annotationRationale: The question combines coordinate triangle area with logarithm operations. The main method uses the equally spaced vertical coordinates, while shoelace provides a distinct general coordinate procedure.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate because the requested quantity is triangle area; logarithm manipulation supports that calculation.

review.questionCheck: The coordinates simplify to (0,1), (u,2), (v,3). Independently, the area is \(\tfrac12|2u-v|=\tfrac12\log_2(9/7)=\log_2(3/\sqrt7)\), confirming choice B. Both supplied reference figures place B correctly to the right of AC at height 2; no contradiction appears.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. LIVE shoelace and Random Math's determinant calculation are retained in shoelace-area. Random Math's rectangle and horizontal-level decompositions are consolidated into the simpler midpoint route. Its cross-product calculation is an equivalent coordinate-area computation with unnecessary extra machinery.
review.annotationCheck: Coordinate area and logarithm operations are appropriately assessed, with elementary logarithm evaluation supporting both routes. The midpoint and triangle-area concepts are correctly method-specific. The source labels preserve third-party status and make no unsupported official-authorship claim.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate because the requested quantity is triangle area; logarithm manipulation supports that calculation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The midpoint of AC is (v/2,2), and 2u-v=log base 2 of 9/7 is positive. Thus BM=u-v/2. The median divides the triangle into two triangles with common horizontal base BM and height 1, giving the claimed area and choice B.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The credit to Random Math's final horizontal-level decomposition is accurate as mathematical inspiration. Introducing the midpoint produces a genuinely reconstructed explanation with original prose; source-informed-original is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The equally spaced vertical coordinates explain the first move. Coordinates, the sign of the base length, the two heights and the final logarithm simplification are all justified without needing another figure.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Coordinate geometry, base-height area, the midpoint instance of internal segment division and logarithm rules are all used. The segment-section node is precise even though only its midpoint case is exercised.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native coordinate-geometry, triangle-area and logarithm-operation links fit. No CN link is supplied for the segment-section refinement.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The partial coordinate links support local length and area work, without establishing four-quadrant modeling or general coordinate proofs. 6.G.A.1 supports decomposition. G-GPE.B.6 is used only in its midpoint case, and F-BF.B.5 only through logarithmic manipulation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The cyclic products reduce correctly to half the absolute value of 2u-v. The logarithm identity gives log base 2 of 9/7>0, correctly removing the absolute value and producing log base 2 of 3/sqrt(7).
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: Correctly credits LIVE's shoelace explanation and Random Math's determinant alternative for this question. The prose and explicit cyclic-product presentation are independently written, with appropriate third-party attribution.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The coordinate simplification motivates the short formula calculation. The shoelace rule is explained at use, and the sign and logarithm transitions are visible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Shoelace and logarithm operations are the exact central concepts. The refined shoelace node appropriately replaces a broad coordinate-area label in this method.
